newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey approves $776 mln sell-offs in March-April.
newsitem.headline: Turkey approves $776 mln sell-offs in March-April.

text.p: Turkey's High Board of Privatisation approved the sale or transfer of companies worth a total $776 million in March and April, the Privatisation Administration (OIB) said on Wednesday.
But of this total, only $28.5 million has so far been paid to the OIB, it said.
The board has approved the 30-year transfer of operating rights for seven ports worth a total $223 million and the sale of stakes in nine companies, the OIB statement said.
The sales of four of these companies has been agreed.

Of these, Ergani Cement was sold to Rumeli Cement for $46.7 million, tyre company Petlas was sold to Kombassan Holding for $35.75 million and stakes in the cement sector companies Cemas and Cimhol were bought by Isiklar Holding for $3.05 million.
Negotiations were continuing on the sale of the maritime transportation company Deniz Nakliyat for $129 million and on the sale of the brick making company Filyos Ates Tuglasi for $18.2 million.
The sale of Etibank for $185 million, Anadolubank for $69.5 million and Denizbank for $66 million was also still under negotiation.
The OIB said in a statement that tenders would be issued in the coming days for the sale of five companies and for the sale of operations and property belonging to three other companies.
The planned block sales will include Kurtalan Cement Industry, Bozuyuk Ceramic Industry, the fruit juice company Meybuz, Sivas Iron and Steel Works and the Black Sea Copper Works, the statement said.

It added that tenders would also be issued for operations owned by Orus Forestry Products Industry, for interests in the textile-to-clothing group Sumer Holding and for operations owned by Meat and Fish Products A.S.
